correctness.rationale: Writing \(a=\|x\|\), \(b=\|y\|\), the triangle inequality makes the numerator at most \((\lambda a+\mu b)^2+(\mu a+\lambda b)^2=(\lambda^2+\mu^2)(a^2+b^2)+4\lambda\mu ab\), and \(2ab\le a^2+b^2\) gives the universal endpoint. If \(J(X)=2\), simultaneous almost-maximal \(\|u+v\|\) and \(\|u-v\|\), together with norming functionals, makes both weighted sums tend to \(\lambda+\mu\), attaining the endpoint as a supremum. Conversely, an endpoint-approaching sequence forces the two input norms to equalize; the total nonnegative triangle-inequality defect tends to zero, so separate norming functionals recover unit vectors with both sum and difference norms tending to two, hence \(J(X)=2\). This does not assume attainment or finite dimension.

final_claim: For every real Banach space \(X\) of dimension at least two and \(\lambda,\mu>0\), \(L_{YJ}(\lambda,\mu,X)\le(\lambda+\mu)^2/(\lambda^2+\mu^2)\); equality holds exactly when the James constant \(J(X)=2\), so strict inequality at this endpoint is equivalent to uniform non-squareness.
limitations: Real Banach spaces and strictly positive parameters only.
